newsitem.title: FRANCE: KAL seeks to boost yields ex-Europe.
newsitem.headline: KAL seeks to boost yields ex-Europe.

text.p: Korean Airlines (KAL)individual cargo stations in continental Europe will have a free hand in implementing measures they deemed appropriate to improve yields, KAL's Paris-based assistant cargo manager, Europe, Denis Lemoin, told Reuters.

This follows a decision by the airline to shelve plans for an autumn increase of five to 10 percent, probably until January 1997, he said. KAL last implemented general increases on ex-Europe rates in April 1996.
"The market was just not strong enough last month. Another important factor is increased capacity from Europe to Korea, either direct or by transhipment, which produced downward pressures on rates,"
However Lemoin said the the past fortnight had seen ex-Europe volumes pick-up with freighter load factors currently running at 95 percent.
In tonnage terms, KAL's ex-Europe traffic, in the first nine months of 1996, was up three percent on 1995 as whole which compared with a 21 percent increase last year in relation to 1994.

KAL's Paris cargo office has taken the step to no longer offer spot prices, which effectively amounted to a five percent increase for certain categories of shipments, said KAL's CDG-based cargo manager France, Christian Prochasson.

Lemoin said European carriers offering "direct" services to Korea had been to the fore in reducing rates while the so-called "second-class" carriers had kept up the tradition of being competitively-priced.
Commenting on the arrival of Asiana Airlines, Lemoin added that thee airline's Boeing 747 freighter and combi services from Amsterdam and Brussels had not lifted cargo capacity significantly.
"Their capacity probably represents about ten percent of our global cargo capacity ex-Europe so we are only talking about a small-volume of shipments being up for grabs." he said..
The only change to KAL's Boeing 747-200F programme from Europe for the forthcoming winter season is an extra, weekly Amsterdam frequency.

KAL operates a total of 13 weekly full-freighter flights from Europe to Seoul leaving from Frankfurt (four weekly), Paris (two), Basle (two), Amsterdam (two), London (one), Brussels (one) and Milan (one). --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
